notes: Passing automated checks does not establish complete factory equivalence or physical operation.
No board flashing or OTA; original dump and archived images remain read-only.
Host assertions include parameter sweeps; their count is not a code-coverage percentage.

platform.scope: Production worker/driver code with deterministic ESP-IDF adapters; no real RF, scheduling, electrical or TLS validation.

frontend.scope: JavaScript syntax and DOM-independent crop/metadata checks; real browser Canvas and guest upload are recorded separately.

wheel_reproduction.reason: No --wheel supplied; controlled archive cases ran offline

qemu_profile.scope: Check the owned Small TV profile against firmware wiring and generic QEMU routing.

approved_fixes.simple-sunday-standard-tm-wday: Display Sun for standard tm_wday 0; factory 0 repeats the date, while factory 7 draws Sun
approved_fixes.analog-perpendicular-stroke-offsets: Use cos/sin for x/y after atan2+pi/2; the original sin/cos collapses axis-aligned thick strokes

machine.scope: Controlled renderer execution; literal LCD/format adapters and separately declared corrected reference; no board/timing claim

machine_control.scope: Exact machine-code timer/slideshow control transitions and LEDC initialization/schedule traces; output boundaries adapted; task scheduling, electrical PWM and pixel decoding unverified here

backlight.approved_fix: photo fade must restore configured duty even when the original schedule cache did not change
backlight.scope: Executed LEDC initialization, duty arithmetic and conditional schedule call traces; successful driver boundaries are captured. RF, electrical PWM and SDK locking are outside scope.

approved_fixes.clip-partially-visible-glyph: Factory 0x4200950e rejects an entire glyph if its rectangle crosses 239; retain its computed bitmap and clip only the visible columns/rows.
approved_fixes.bounded-clean-classic-fields: City/title/icon cleanup and bounded field glyphs; overflowing labels start at the left scroll endpoint. Later motion is a requested extension, tested separately.

machine_classic.scope: Exact executed classic text/window pixels and media-request identities; media output is recorded, not decoded. Executed animation cursor/header selection; task scheduling and physical timing remain outside scope.

machine_weather.scope: Both real BMP decoders and LCD pixels; flash/allocation/mutex boundaries adapted. JPEG output remains recorded. Incremental native pixels compared with fresh rendering and a separately declared corrected factory reference. Scroll frames checked against factory bitmaps and independent phase expectations; injected real-decoder read failures. Only explicit status-update events and active 100-ms scroll steps are modeled here.

machine_calendar.scope: Both actual RV32 renderers, all framebuffer pixels on calendar/year/yday-collision jumps with unchanged seconds/minutes and long-to-short date changes. Corrected original invalidates its previous-second cache and raises the missing minute-refresh flag on calendar changes, maps Sunday 0 to supported 7 and clears the simple date band. No SNTP transport or physical timing claim.

machine_jpeg.scope: Actual RV32 JPEG input, Huffman/IDCT/color conversion, output callbacks and LCD blitters; SDK flash/allocation/mutex and LCD transport only are adapted. All 57600 pixels compared; clipped placement uses independently placed pixels from the actual factory decoder. Factory flash callback error is executed literally; native failure erasure is a declared correction. No physical or throughput claim.

machine_timezones.scope:
Execute real RV32 timezone code and libc against independently loaded IANA TZif.

Factory libc receives its literal recovered strings; discrepancies are retained.
Only environment, libc reentrancy/locking and existing LCD adapters are replaced.
Date conversion, TZ parsing, transition search and calendar arithmetic execute
from immutable ELF bytes. No SNTP transport or physical-board claim is made.

machine_time_state.scope:
Execute factory time/cache/retry instructions and compiled native sync validity.

Calendar conversion and both notification handlers are actual RV32 code.
Only factory time(), SNTP restart and logging SDK boundaries are adapted.
This gate does not substitute for the separate real UDP/SNTP QEMU test.

machine_network.scope:
Execute original and rebuilt RV32 station events and the original active loop.

Synthetic DHCP leases and Wi-Fi events enter the actual compiled handlers. SDK
connect/notification/HTTP lifecycle and IPv4 formatting are boundaries; field
selection, cache, counters and native address formatting remain machine code.
The bounded original main-loop slice records dispatch, without substituting its
branches. This is not a radio, whole FreeRTOS scheduler or live QEMU link test.

machine_text.scope: Execute real text/UTF-8 RV32 code against independent BDF and factory bitmap data.

qemu.scope: Real firmware boot/reset/DHCP/SNTP, localhost HTTP, synthetic weather, natural calendar/DST transitions and complete instruction-replayed frames. The separate unsynchronized scene similarity remains diagnostic. No physical hardware or Internet weather service.

startup_wait.scope: Measure the first native clock frame after an actual UDP SNTP notification.

weather_wait.scope: Observe real clock frames while an external weather server withholds its reply.

scan.reason: Confirmed vendor /scan zero-result null dereference at 0x4200f484; native scan is a required check

http_initial_setup.scope: Real HTTP/TCP, open synthetic Wi-Fi, DHCP, raw settings persistence, reboot and SNTP; no browser JS, real RF or WPA handshake.

weather_http.scope: Real guest DNS/TCP/HTTP via isolated loopback fixture; parsed synthetic weather and stable LCD regions. No Internet service, physical RF or full-program equivalence.

time_http.scope:
Exercise actual UDP SNTP fallback, clock updates and displayed dates in QEMU.

QMP changes only the opt-in service's responses. Guest registers, RAM, clocks and
executable bytes are never patched. Initial flash changes are synthetic settings
in disposable copies; both production applications and source images stay intact.

text_http.scope: Exercise actual UTF-8 settings/weather HTTP and bounded text pixels in both VMs.

factory_utf8_city_fault.scope: Expected immutable factory defect only; no corrected-program panic is permitted.

regional_http.scope:
Verify regional keys through actual HTTP, raw flash, weather and clock rendering.

Only synthetic settings and external HTTP/NTP responses are supplied. All guest
code is immutable; QMP observes identified fields and never patches guest memory.
The unchanged factory raw ABI and the native NVS ABI are deliberately separate.

calendar_http.scope:
Follow natural calendar/DST transitions from real NTP packets to complete LCD frames.

Only synthetic HTTP settings and external NTP/weather responses are supplied.
Hardware breakpoints and bounded reads observe immutable running programs.
Independent pinned IANA TZif and real factory RV32 renderers form the references.

completed_scenes.scope:
Compare completed real QEMU frames with immutable RV32 instruction replay.

Hardware breakpoints observe renderer entry/return. No guest instruction,
register, flag or RAM value is written. Real decoded media and all 57,600 pixels
are compared; time/animation differences and declared factory fixes stay explicit.

normalized.scope: Complete RGB565 frames, real media decoders, same canonical inputs and explicit factory corrections.

field_http.scope: Real guest HTTP/cache and exact city/title/icon pixels with immutable factory bitmaps, guard strips, scroll directions/pauses and blocked refresh/theme reset. QMP observations briefly pause/resume execution; no memory/register/program patches. Literal factory differences recorded separately. No physical timing or whole-program identity.

not_applicable_factory: corrected cleanup expectations; literal pixels recorded

not_run.name: hardware_browser_soak
not_run.reason: Physical board/RF/live weather service, long-run memory and full browser acceptance remain manual; focused browser regression is recorded separately
